title: Oncall quickfire log — Vikram 2026-03-28
content:
Quick notes from 06:00-14:00 shift. Unpolished, mostly for handoff and follow-ups.

Summary:
- Pager flurry from 06:12–07:05: sustained p99 latency spikes on serving-runtime-prod cluster (eu-west).
- Mitigations applied: temporary target-rollout to model-x-small (v1.9) for route /v1/chat, scaled down model-gpu pool instance group, forced KV-cache warmup on a subset of nodes.
- Secondary: single node in dedicated-pool-3 reported disk pressure (kubelet) at 10:40 — cordoned and drained, replaced.

Timeline + notes:
- 06:12 ALERT: Alert: SVC-LAT-P99 > 1200ms for 5m (route: chat-gen /v1/chat). Pager: phone, slack #sre-oncall.
  - First look: metrics show CPU on serving-runtime-pod-abc-0 at 98% and host load spiking; mem stable.
  - kubectl (quick): kubectl -n serving-runtime get pods -o wide | egrep "serve|model"
  - logs: kubectl -n serving-runtime logs pod/serve-abc-0 -c runtime | tail -n 200 | egrep "KVCache|compile|OOM|latency"
  - Found repeated 'loading model weights' and 'kernel compile fallback' messages — points at JIT/kernel-selection thrash during rollout.

- 06:25 Mitigation 1: Temporarily route 30% traffic to model-x-small (v1.9) across eu-west via routing API. Observed p99 drop to ~420ms in 2 mins.
  - Command used: curl -X POST https://control-plane.local/api/v1/routing -d '{"route":"/v1/chat","policy":"split","weights":{"model-x-small":0.3,"model-x":0.7}}' (sanitized here).

- 06:33 Mitigation 2: Triggered kv-cache-warmup on 4/6 nodes as emergency measure. Warmup logs show successful prefix caches for most popular prompts. p95 stable, p99 improving.

- 07:02 Further investigation: Canary model rollout had new quantization kernels (PR: GitHub:pr/rdw/optimizer-fix) that cause heavy compile activity on first N requests. Likely correlation.
  - Action: Rollback canary; paused further rollouts.
  - Follow-up: ask runtime team to add background precompile during deploy for models with new kernel sets.

Secondary incident:
- 10:40 ALERT: Node pressure (disk) on dedicated-pool-3/node-12. kubelet eviction at 10:38.
  - Actions: cordon node-12, drain with --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data, respawn replacements.
  - Note: local /var/lib/model-cache filled due to old cache cleanup job failing (cron job model-cache-prune).
  - TODO: fix model-cache-prune job (see below).

Follow-ups / Runbook TODOs (write these into runbook section later):
1) Add "precompile kernels" step to model rollout checklist (owner: Research infra — Samir, due 2026-04-04).
2) Add alert: "sustained kernel-compile CPU spike" (rule: CPU% > 70 for 3m AND logs contain 'kernel compile' string) so we don't rely solely on latency signals. (owner: eng-observability — Maya, due 2026-04-01).
3) Update runbook: explicit step to rollback canary on compile-thrash patterns + command snippets (kubectl, routing API payload). (owner: me, due 2026-03-30).
4) Fix cron job model-cache-prune: investigate why it missed cycles on dedicated-pool-3 (ticket: RDW-5821). (owner: infra — Priya, due 2026-03-31).
5) Add task to add eviction-safe local cache path sizing and monitoring for dedicated pools. (owner: platform-eng — TBD).

Notes to self (investigation bits):
- Check kernel compile cache hit-rate around the incident window: prometheus metric runtime_kernel_cache_hits vs misses. Metric: runtime_kernel_cache_miss_total{cluster="eu-west"}.
- Check git tag of canary: git rev-list --no-walk --max-count=1 <pr-branch> (PR linked above).
- Look at the model artifact size difference between v1.9 and the canary (maybe extra operator libs).

Manual commands I ran (copying here so next oncall can replicate):
- kubectl -n serving-runtime get pods -o wide | egrep "serve|model"
- kubectl -n serving-runtime logs pod/serve-abc-0 -c runtime --since=15m | egrep "compile|kernel|error"
- curl -sS https://observability.local/api/query?query=runtime_kernel_cache_miss_total | jq .
- control-plane routing change (sanitized): curl -X POST https://control-plane.local/api/v1/routing -d '{"route":"/v1/chat","policy":"split","weights":{"model-x-small":0.3,"model-x":0.7}}'
- cordon+drain: kubectl cordon node-12 && kubectl drain node-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=10m

Handover summary for next oncall (14:00 shift):
- Major incident mitigated, rollback in place. Keep monitoring p99 on /v1/chat for next 12h. If p99 > 800ms for 10m, escalate to runtime-leads (Samir/Maya) + open INC-2026-1135 postmortem draft.
- Ensure model-cache-prune cron fixed and dedicated-pool-3 node replaced — confirm disk pressure alert cleared.
- Add a small note in #sre-runbooks when you push the runbook updates (I will draft later today).

Loose thoughts / questions to capture before I forget:
- Could we have a pre-deploy smoke that exercises kernel paths (low-cost synthetic requests) to avoid first-request compiles? Would reduce p99 cliffs.
- Consider adding a short TTL to new kernel artifacts to evict old versions more aggressively on limited nodes.

Quick TODO (my priority):
- [ ] Draft runbook change text (rollback + precompile steps) — target EOD 2026-03-28.
- [ ] Create RDW ticket for model-cache-prune failing job (RDW-5821) and add owner tag.
- [ ] Ping runtime team about background precompile prototype (Samir).

End handoff. Next: add these items to Confluence/Runbook and tag runtime and observability teams.

Raw scratch: slack refs: #sre-oncall, #runtime-alerts, #prod-ops. Pager: INC-2026-1135.

-- Vikram
